questions.q: What is the Neo4j Graph Data Science (GDS) library?
options: An official, separate Neo4j plugin providing 65+ graph algorithms as callable Cypher procedures
A built-in part of core Cypher requiring no additional installation
A third-party, unofficial tool not maintained by Neo4j
A replacement for Cypher that uses entirely different query syntax
questions.explain: GDS is an official plugin, installed alongside the core database, adding a large library of algorithms called via ordinary Cypher CALL syntax.

questions.q: Why is GDS implemented as a separate plugin rather than built directly into core Cypher?
options: GDS algorithms need to iterate over the entire graph repeatedly, a fundamentally different access pattern from Cypher's MATCH-a-pattern-and-return workload
Neo4j intentionally limits core Cypher's feature set for licensing reasons unrelated to performance
Graph algorithms cannot technically be expressed using Cypher's CALL syntax
There is no real reason — it's an arbitrary packaging decision
questions.explain: The lesson explains this as an architectural distinction: iterative, whole-graph algorithms benefit from their own specialized in-memory representation.

questions.q: What is a graph projection in the context of GDS?
options: A compact, in-memory copy of the nodes, relationships, and properties an algorithm needs, held separately from the main graph store
A permanent transformation that replaces the original graph data on disk
A visual diagram exported for presentations
A backup copy of the entire database, including all indexes
questions.explain: The projection is an in-memory structure built specifically for efficient iterative algorithm execution, separate from the main disk-backed graph.

questions.q: What is the difference between GDS's 'stream' mode and 'write' mode?
options: Stream returns results directly without modifying the graph; write persists results back to the graph as new node properties
Stream and write are identical, differing only in naming
Write mode never returns any results at all
Stream mode permanently deletes the graph projection after running
questions.explain: Stream is for exploration without side effects; write persists results so later Cypher queries can use them like ordinary properties.

questions.q: After running `CALL gds.pageRank.write('employeeGraph', {writeProperty: 'pageRankScore'})`, how would you use the results in a later query?
options: With an ordinary Cypher query like `MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name ORDER BY p.pageRankScore DESC`, since the score was written back as a normal node property
You would need to re-run the GDS algorithm every time you want to read a score
The results are only accessible through a separate GDS-specific query language
Write mode does not actually store anything usable afterward
questions.explain: Write mode persists the algorithm's output as a real property on the nodes, so it becomes queryable with plain MATCH/RETURN/ORDER BY like any other property.
